items.title: Crabka vs Strimzi on GKE: multi-node clusters + client resilience, zero-copy fetch (sendfile/kTLS), decode-free produce
items.body:
## Summary

Gets Crabka running as a real **multi-broker cluster against Strimzi on GKE**, benchmarks the two like-for-like, and closes the gaps the benchmark exposed. In scope:

- **Multi-node KRaft quorum + client resilience** so Crabka works against real Kafka/Strimzi (goal #1).
- A **zero-copy fetch path** — `sendfile(2)` on plaintext, **Linux kTLS** on encrypted connections.
- A **decode-free produce path** — append the producer's batch verbatim, no decode/re-encode, no decompress.
- **Multi-listener fixes** the TLS path exposed.
- The GKE cluster + full reproduction recipe **as checked-in Terraform**.

All broker changes keep `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and are Kafka-wire byte-exact (golden + JVM-differential tested).

## What's here

**Multi-node clusters that work against real Kafka (goal #1).** The operator now renders `controller_quorum_voters` and the broker accepts it, with controller-listener mTLS, so a 3-node KRaft quorum actually elects; a broker killed mid-election re-bootstraps instead of crashlooping. On the client side: coordinator discovery, producer **failover to the re-elected leader** (with fast detection), hostname-address resolution so multi-broker produce routes, and a bootstrap fallback so a consumer reaches its group coordinator even when that broker isn't a separately dialable address.

**Benchmark harness + GKE comparison.** Apples-to-apples resource capture from Prometheus (cgroup working-set + the Strimzi JVM heap/non-heap split), a `pd-ssd` storage path, larger scenarios (`firehose`, `datarate-512k`), and a TLS data-path benchmark. Both stacks get byte-for-byte identical pod resources; brokers run one cluster at a time.

**Reproducible as code.** [`bench/terraform/gke/`](bench/terraform/gke) provisions the exact GKE cluster — `e2-standard-4` / COS / `pd-ssd`, two node pools (brokers one-per-node + a lighter pool for operators/Prometheus/driver) — verified **no-drift** against the live cluster via `tofu import` + `plan`. Its [README](bench/terraform/gke/README.md) is the full provision → install operators + Prometheus → run the matrix → aggregate recipe.

**Zero-copy fetch** (each increment byte-exact):
- `TCP_NODELAY` + 1 MiB socket buffers
- fetch write-plan + vectored write (removes 3 of 4 fetch copies)
- **`sendfile(2)`** zero-copy fetch (plaintext) — page-cache → NIC, exactly as Apache Kafka
- cross-platform sendfile (macOS/BSD via `nix`; Windows `TransmitFile` deferred — `unsafe` vs the workspace `forbid`)
- **Linux kTLS** — `sendfile` *through* TLS via kernel-offloaded encryption (`ktls` crate + rustls secret extraction; startup probe gates the per-connection path)

io_uring was evaluated and rejected (no native tokio bridge; Kafka itself uses sendfile).

**Decode-free produce:**
- **verbatim passthrough** — append the producer's batch bytes; patch only `base_offset`/`partition_leader_epoch` (both outside the CRC region → no recompute)
- **skip the owned `ProduceRequest` decode** on the verbatim path — stop LZ4-decompressing batches the broker stores compressed (the profiled produce-side hotspot)
- `append_verbatim` writes the body without a full-payload copy

**Multi-listener fixes** (never benchmarked before): the TLS data listener collided with the fixed `9093` controller port (→ `9094`); the topic reconciler defaulted to `"PLAIN"` not the declared `"plain"`; and **metadata wasn't listener-aware** — fixed across `Metadata` / `DescribeCluster` / `FindCoordinator` so a TLS client gets the TLS endpoint and a plaintext client gets the plaintext one.

## Results (GKE, 3 brokers, pd-ssd, single sample/cell)

- Crabka **matches or beats** Strimzi on produce-and-consume — wins multi-producer fan-out, level on small-record and `acks=all`, within ~6% on 100 KiB — while a broker's container working set sits in the **low hundreds of MiB** vs Strimzi's **2.5–5.5 GiB** (**9–37× lighter**), at **1.6–3.0× more messages per CPU-core**.
- `sendfile` + the produce **decode-skip** lifted large-msg from ~75% to ~94% of Strimzi's throughput at ~⅓ the CPU; the residual gap is per-batch **service rate**, not the copy.
- **kTLS validated on GKE** (COS auto-loads the `tls` module; the broker logs *"Linux kTLS supported…"*) and byte-exact — **Crabka TLS throughput == plaintext** (zero copy preserved through encryption).
- Post-rebase matrix re-run (`fix19`): **no regression**.

Full per-increment detail + tables: [`benchmark_status.md`](benchmark_status.md), [`bench/results/`](bench/results/).

## Docs

A new website benchmark page ([Crabka vs Strimzi](website/content/benchmarks/crabka-vs-strimzi.md)) and the README performance section, re-based on the Kubernetes numbers; the outdated single-node Crabka-vs-Kafka benchmark (page + local harness + hero graphic) removed and the homepage re-based onto the GKE comparison. Public docs state current-state facts only; the journey lives in `benchmark_status.md`.

## Test status

`cargo build` / `clippy -D warnings` clean on Linux, macOS, and Windows; broker / protocol / log / client unit + integration suites pass, including new verbatim / sendfile / kTLS / listener-aware / coordinator-fallback coverage. kTLS byte-exactness validated live on WSL2 + GKE. The coordinator change is the client-side bootstrap fallback the pool already documents (no broker behavior change), so `ip_quotas` and the rest of the broker suite are unaffected.

## Follow-up

- Sharper kTLS demo (an on/off toggle + a bandwidth-bound scenario) so the matrix *separates* kTLS from userspace TLS rather than only proving it adds zero overhead.
- Deeper produce service-rate profiling to chase full large-msg parity.

items.title: Optimize pipeline: JSON serialization, two-pass solving, EKF tuning
items.body:
## Summary

Performance and quality improvements to the MLAT pipeline:

**Serialization optimization:** Replaced `ostringstream`-based JSON serialization with `snprintf`/direct string concatenation in `format_double`, `to_json_fix`, `to_json_track`, and `group_json_object`. Added 64KB output buffers to both binaries. This eliminates hundreds of thousands of heap allocations per run.

**Two-pass solving:** Groups that fail with `no_prior_2sensor` (2 sensors but no cached position prior) are now buffered during the first pass and retried after the position cache is populated. Recovers ~694 additional L4 solves.

**EKF tuning:** Adjusted measurement noise model (floor 500→700, ceiling 3000→5000, GDOP multiplier 3→4.5), prediction-aided solver relaxation (max_residual cap 500→800, offset 5000→8000), and Chi-squared gate (21.11→25.0).

**Results on 1-hour benchmark (165,917 groups):**

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|--------|--------|-------|--------|
| Wall time | 5.30s | 4.20s | **-20.8%** |
| L4 solve rate | 52.2% | 52.7% | +0.5pp |
| L4 median residual | 18.19m | 18.08m | improved |
| L5 accept rate | 55.3% | 59.0% | **+3.7pp** |
| L5 outputs | 85,526 | 91,382 | **+6.8%** |
| Tracks | 120 | 120 | same |

Zero quality degradation — residuals maintained or improved.

**README** updated with current benchmark numbers, PGO instructions, and cleaned up outdated info.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Run benchmark on your hardware: `cat data-pipe/correlation_groups_1h.jsonl | ./native-l45/build/mlat-solver-native 2>solver.log | ./native-l45/build/track-builder-native 2>tracker.log > /dev/null` — verify L4 solve rate ≥52%, L5 accept rate ≥55%
- [ ] Verify JSON output is parseable: pipe L5 output through `python3 -c "import json,sys; [json.loads(l) for l in sys.stdin]"`
- [ ] Test live map replay: pipe through `python3 live-map/server.py` and verify aircraft appear with correct details
- [ ] Review EKF parameter changes in `track.cpp` — the Chi2 gate increase (21→25) is the most aggressive change; verify on your production data that it doesn't admit too many false positives
- [ ] Test with GCC 11 as well (the `-fno-math-errno` flag is supported by both GCC 11 and 13)

### Notes

- The two-pass solver adds second_pass stats to the L4 log output (deferred count and solved count)
- All changes tested end-to-end including live map visualization with 120 aircraft
- PGO build instructions added to README section 5.4

items.body:
Addresses the remaining open items in the analytics module: one missing test, stale performance numbers, and an outdated public-API inventory.

## Changes

### `tests/analytics/test_olap_lru_cache.cpp` — AC-9 (new)
Adds `OLAPLRUCache.BoundedMemoryGrowthUnder10000UniqueQueries`: the last open Phase 4 requirement. Runs 10 000 queries against a cache capped at 100 entries; asserts `execution_time_ms >= 0.0` on every result, then re-executes the tail-100 to confirm correctness after eviction.

```cpp
OLAPEngine::Config cfg;
cfg.result_cache_max_entries = 100;
OLAPEngine engine(cfg);
for (int i = 0; i < 10'000; ++i) {
    OLAPResult r = engine.execute(makeSimpleQuery("collection_" + std::to_string(i)));
    ASSERT_GE(r.execution_time_ms, 0.0) << "invalid result at query " << i;
}
```

items.title: docs: update write RPS benchmarks to 10k+
items.body:
This PR updates the benchmark documentation to reflect the improved write throughput introduced by commit `d2d0e61`. With the new appendable WAL, drain-loop batching, and buffer pooling, write performance now exceeds 10k RPS under Vegeta load testing. The documentation is updated to surface this improvement clearly.

## Problem Statement
- Existing benchmark docs and README still reported ~3k write RPS.
- After recent WAL and batching optimizations, the documented numbers were outdated.
- There was no guidance or reference for higher-rate Vegeta benchmark runs.

## Solution
- Added updated benchmark artifacts representing 10k+ write RPS.
- Included a Vegeta benchmark script for higher-rate testing.
- Updated documentation to clearly show the new throughput and how it was measured.
- Ensured readers understand that the benchmarks correspond to the post-`d2d0e61` implementation.

## Changes Made

### 1. Benchmark Data Update
- Added new Vegeta benchmark results under `docs/benchmarks/`.
- Included representative results demonstrating sustained 10k+ write RPS.
- Kept formatting consistent with existing benchmark files.

### 2. Benchmark Script
- Added a Vegeta test script (`vegeta_10k_test.sh`) for high-throughput write testing.
- Script can be reused by contributors to reproduce or validate results.

### 3. Documentation Updates
- Updated `docs/benchmarks/` to include the new write throughput data.
- Updated `README.md` to reflect:
  - Improved write RPS numbers.
  - Reference to the updated benchmark results.
  - Context that the gains come from WAL batching and buffer pooling.

## Benchmark Context
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Vegeta Load Test] --> B[HTTP Write Requests]
    B --> C[Appendable WAL]
    C --> D[Drain-loop Batching]
    D --> E[Buffer Pooling]
    E --> F[10k+ Write RPS]
```
closes #16

items.title: docs: fix README inaccuracies, extract build docs, elevate Docker/Kubernetes deployment, update benchmarks
items.body:
README had several inaccuracies and buried the recommended deployment path. Build/test instructions were inline rather than in a dedicated doc. Benchmark numbers were significantly outdated and additional inaccuracies were found across the repo's example files.

## Inaccuracies fixed
- **Go minimum version**: `1.21` → `1.25` (aligns with `go.mod`)
- **`-cache-ttl` default**: `5m` → `0` (actual code default; LRU-only, no TTL)
- **`GET /admin/workers`**: was incorrectly documented as unauthenticated — it calls `extractBearerToken` and requires a valid Bearer token
- **Security Model table**: `/admin/schemas` is public; only `/admin/workers` requires auth — table previously said both required a token
- **Routing description**: README and `examples/02` both claimed "round-robins" — the actual code uses cache-aware routing (`FindWorkerForEntity`) with a least-loaded fallback (`FindLeastLoadedWorker`). Corrected in both places.
- **`curl /admin/workers` examples**: 4 examples (README + `examples/01`, `02`, `04`) were missing the required Bearer token. All updated to obtain a token via `POST /api/login` first.
- **`examples/02` login body**: Was using `{"username":"admin","password":"admin"}` — the actual API accepts `{"client_id":"..."}`. Fixed to match the real API.

## Benchmark results updated
Ran `pytest tests/test_benchmarks.py -v --benchmark-sort=mean` against live workers. The previous numbers were ~25× too pessimistic and have been replaced with actual measured values:

| Benchmark | Mean latency | Throughput |
|-----------|-------------|------------|
| REST PUT (sequential, warm) | ~1 ms | ~1,000 ops/s |
| REST GET (warm cache, sequential) | ~1 ms | ~1,000 ops/s |
| REST PUT→GET round-trip | ~2 ms | ~520 ops/s |
| gRPC PUT (proc-worker direct) | ~0.6 ms | ~1,700 ops/s |
| gRPC GET (warm cache, proc-worker) | ~0.3 ms | ~3,500 ops/s |
| Concurrent PUT (32 threads × 20 each) | — | ~910 ops/s total |
| Concurrent GET (32 threads × 25 each) | — | ~970 ops/s total |
| Bulk write 1000 entities | ~1 s total | ~1,000 ops/s |

## Build docs extracted → `BUILDING.md`
- Created `BUILDING.md` with prerequisites (Go 1.25+), build commands, unit tests, and full Python integration test suite
- README "Building from Source" and "Testing" sections replaced with short references to `BUILDING.md`
- Standalone Prerequisites section removed from README (covered in `BUILDING.md`)

## Docker / Kubernetes highlighted as recommended deployment
- New **"Recommended Deployment: Docker / Kubernetes"** section added at position 3 in the TOC (immediately after Architecture)
- Scenario table links each deployment option with Kubernetes + HPA marked ⭐ recommended for production
- One-liner quick-start: `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose/docker-compose.all-in-one.yml up`
- "Quick Start" renamed to "Quick Start (Local / Development)" to make its scope explicit
- Old "Containerization Examples" section removed — fully superseded by the new prominent section

### [`v1.16.0-pre.3`](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/releases/tag/v1.16.0-pre.3): 1.16.0-pre.3

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/compare/1.16.0-pre.2...1.16.0-pre.3)

## Summary of Changes

**Major Changes:**

-   BGP: New BGP APIs can be used to configure Cilium BGP Control Plane. ([#​32426](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32426), [@​harsimran-pabla](https://togithub.com/harsimran-pabla))
-   NAT source port metrics & table ([#​32152](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32152), [@​tommyp1ckles](https://togithub.com/tommyp1ckles))

**Minor Changes:**

-   Add `CiliumNodeConfig` CRD on API v2 ([#​31721](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/31721), [@​doniacld](https://togithub.com/doniacld))
-   Added a new annotation `ingress.cilium.io/loadbalancer-class` to control the `LoadBalancerClass` of a dedicated LB via the ingress. ([#​31650](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/31650), [@​Sh4d1](https://togithub.com/Sh4d1))
-   cilium-envoy now uses upstream filter chains for L7 LB policy enforcement. ([#​32119](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32119), [@​jrajahalme](https://togithub.com/jrajahalme))
-   CiliumEnvoyConfig CRDs now support an optional 'ports' field in services objects, limiting the redirected service frontends to the ones whose port is listed. ([#​32382](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32382), [@​jrajahalme](https://togithub.com/jrajahalme))
-   CiliumNetworkPolicies are now validated by the operator and the result set in the object's Status field. ([#​32727](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32727), [@​squeed](https://togithub.com/squeed))
-   Do not include the unnecessary "localhost" SAN in autogenerated clustermesh admin certificates ([#​32662](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32662), [@​giorio94](https://togithub.com/giorio94))
-   gateway-api: ALPN support ([#​32486](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32486), [@​rauanmayemir](https://togithub.com/rauanmayemir))
-   Generate SBOMs using Syft instead of bom ([#​32307](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32307), [@​ferozsalam](https://togithub.com/ferozsalam))
-   Helm: Add new value \`.Values.clustermesh.apiserver.tls.enableSecrets. Setting this value to false will disable the creation of TLS certificate secrets for clustermesh, enabling out-of-band TLS certificate secret management. ([#​32196](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32196), [@​soggiest](https://togithub.com/soggiest))
-   Hubble peer's port number is inferred from the agent's configuration instead of assuming defaults ([#​32729](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32729), [@​AwesomePatrol](https://togithub.com/AwesomePatrol))
-   hubble: add SNAT IP flow field and filter ([#​32130](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32130), [@​kaworu](https://togithub.com/kaworu))
-   hubble: add support to filter Hubble flow by network interface. ([#​32286](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32286), [@​kaworu](https://togithub.com/kaworu))
-   hubble: add the cluster name to a flow's source and destination endpoints ([#​32313](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32313), [@​rolinh](https://togithub.com/rolinh))
-   Improved background resynchronization of nodes. Before all nodes were being updated at the same time, now we spread updates over time to average out CPU usage. ([#​32577](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32577), [@​marseel](https://togithub.com/marseel))
-   ingress: request timeout control via operator flag & annotation ([#​31693](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/31693), [@​a5r0n](https://togithub.com/a5r0n))
-   Introduce CLI commands to troubleshoot connectivity issues to the etcd kvstore and clustermesh control plane ([#​32336](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32336), [@​giorio94](https://togithub.com/giorio94))
-   ipsec: Improve CPU usage of cilum-agent in large clusters ([#​32588](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32588), [@​marseel](https://togithub.com/marseel))
-   KVStoreMesh: expose remote clusters information and introduce dedicated CLI command ([#​32156](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32156), [@​giorio94](https://togithub.com/giorio94))
-   Make the overwriting behavior of install-plugins.sh configurable. ([#​32016](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32016), [@​jingyuanliang](https://togithub.com/jingyuanliang))
-   Operator: expose remote clusters information through dedicated CLI command, and introduce troubleshoot commands ([#​32436](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32436), [@​giorio94](https://togithub.com/giorio94))
-   pkg/healthv2: reduce unecessary healthv2 debug log volume. ([#​32319](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32319), [@​tommyp1ckles](https://togithub.com/tommyp1ckles))
-   Report estimated expiry timers for connection-based FQDN entries ([#​32013](https://togithub.com/cilium/cilium/issues/32013), [@​joestringer](https://togithub.com/joestringer))
-   Runtime device detection and subsequent datapath reconfiguration is now the default and only mode of operation.
